tweet_summary: User shares a 5-Minute Crafts-style video demonstrating a pizza-box-folding hack that converts the box into a smaller storage container for leftover slices, captioned 'I was today years old when I found out you could do this…'.
why_note_decision: The tweet is a lifestyle hack demo. The hack is real — some Domino's boxes have perforations specifically for this. The note's claims ('difficult to execute', 'doesn't stay sealed', 'mangles slices') are opinion / mixed-utility critique, not factual debunk. Many replies share the same opinion but that doesn't make the tweet misleading — the video plainly shows the hack working. Community correctly tagged notHelpfulNoteNotNeeded + notHelpfulOpinionSpeculation.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet makes no checkable misleading claim — sharing a lifestyle hack with the caption 'I just learned this' is not misinformation. A note critiquing the hack's utility is opinion/speculation and a clear false positive.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The pizza box folding hack is difficult to execute with thick cardboard, doesn't stay sealed without tape, and mangles the slices.
